answer: The protocol assigns each new agent an inlet token that must be bonded to a kernel contract; the token’s saffron‑colored proof of work is calibrated so that the first identity of a node receives weight 1, while any additional identities derived from the same IP receive weight 1⁄n², where n is the number of identities. When a request is made, the verifier aggregates weighted votes and discards any contribution whose cumulative weight falls below a threshold, forcing an attacker to purchase a full‑weight inlet token for each useful fake identity.
